description:
### Summary

`mount()` and `app.mount()` remove the mount prefix from the request path and forward the rest to the mounted application. Two mistakes in that step let a crafted request reach a route of the mounted application that the outer application protects with path-scoped middleware, such as an authentication check on `/app/admin/*`. The outer application routes on the original path, so the middleware does not run.

title: Hono: RegExpRouter skips wildcard middleware for some route sets and for paths with an encoded line terminator
description:
### Summary

RegExpRouter, which the default `SmartRouter` selects for most applications, skipped wildcard middleware in three cases, so a route handler ran without the middleware registered for it:

1. Middleware whose parameter is written with the explicit default pattern, such as `/api/:tenant{[^/]+}/admin/*`, was not applied to a route written as `/api/:tenant/admin/:id`. (since 4.13.0)
2. Middleware on `/admin/*` was not applied to a route registered on `/admin*` for paths under `/admin/`.

title: @grpc/grpc-js: safe_regex incorrectly applies partial string matching for patterns with alternation
description:
### Summary

The StringMatcher/PathMatcher for `safe_regex` builds its RE2 as `^${regex}$` with no surrounding group. Because alternation has the lowest precedence, a pattern `"a|b|c"` compiles to `/^a|b|c$/` -- "starts with a" OR "contains b" OR "ends with c" instead of a full match of the whole value. title: CVE-2026-122146 - A weakness has been identified in 101arrowz fflate up to 0.8.3. This issue affects the function unzi
description: A weakness has been identified in 101arrowz fflate up to 0.8.3. This issue affects the function unzipSync of the file esm/index.mjs. This manipulation causes uncontrolled memory allocation. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. It is suggested to update the configuration settings. The maintainer disputes this issue as a vulnerability. The library is a pure JavaScript decompressor that allocates memory proportional to the decompressed payload size, which is expected behavior. Excessive allocations simply throw a standard JavaScript RangeError or reach engine heap limits. Furthermore, because a low-level decompression library cannot distinguish between a maliciously crafted compression bomb and a legitimate file with a high compression ratio, the API explicitly provides a filter option allowing callers to restrict decompressed file sizes and prevent denial-of-service according to their application's requirements, as seen both in the documentation and noted in the reported issue.
